items.response: Sending the Hannah text now. For Olivia, I'll keep the Instant Payouts v1 blurb to what merchants get and leave out any date, since Aisha hasn't signed off on one; if a timeline is needed it says 'target' only. I'll write it in your style, short, no em dashes, 'merchant' not 'customer', and say EFT where payouts are mentioned, not wire. Action: send the Hannah text, pull the v1 scope from the rollout doc, and put a 4-5 line draft for Olivia in your drafts, unsent, for you to review.

I don't have your pickup time for next Friday, so I can't give you an exact arrival yet. Ottawa from Leslieville is about 4 h 35 min without traffic (452 km), but leaving after pickup means you'd hit Friday traffic on the 401, so add a buffer on top, plus the Big Apple stop in Colborne that Leo counts as a rule. Action: ask what time pickup ends, then work out a realistic arrival at Grace and Daniel's with traffic and the stop, and give you that.

Sam's birthday is March 22 and he'd rather have a quiet dinner at home than a party, so I'd plan a cosy vegetarian dinner (no fish or seafood) with a gift that isn't scented, since strong fragrances give him migraines, so no candles, soap or perfume. For the anniversary on June 16 (dinner for two on Tue 2026-06-16), restaurant reservations open in April, and your shortlist is Edulis, Ascari Enoteca and Planta Queen, which has vegetarian options. You'll also need a sitter for Leo: Maya R. ($20/h), Josie T. ($22/h) or Ana P. ($17/h). Action: put a reminder in April to book the anniversary dinner and ask a sitter, and ask you what Sam's been into lately so I can suggest a few gift ideas.

That sounds like a lovely birthday for your mom, and the flowers clearly landed. I'll hold the Priya book decision until tonight. Action: add your mom's birthday (November 3) to the calendar as a yearly event with a reminder a week before, and note the Mumbai florist so it's easy to repeat next year.

I don't have the start date for this year's Leslieville Farmers' Market saved, so I don't want to guess. Action: look up the market's 2026 season dates and hours and report back, then offer to add opening day to the calendar.

Congratulations, Riya the godmother, that's wonderful! Ira born February 14, 2026 in Vancouver, a Valentine's baby. Action: add Ira's birthday (February 14) to the calendar as a yearly event with a reminder a week before, like your other family birthdays, and when you have a moment I can also ask you for Mei's birthday since I don't have it yet.

The Leslieville Farmers' Market opens Sun 10 May (Mother's Day) and runs Sundays 9:00 to 14:00 at Jonathan Ashbridge Park, 1515 Queen St E, through 25 October. Action: offer to add opening day to your calendar.

Done on both counts. I'll switch the out-of-office off for tomorrow morning and change the message to something like: 'Hi, I'm back in the office but still catching up on email, so replies may take a little longer. If it's urgent, please let me know. Best, Riya'. Action: turn the auto-reply off for tomorrow morning, update the message with that wording, and show you the final text to confirm.

Got it, congrats on it being confirmed. I'll add the Lumen Pay quarterly planning offsite on 2026-11-12 at the Gladstone House, 9:00 am to 6:00 pm. Action: create the calendar event and check whether anything else that day clashes, then tell you if it does.

Sending the reply to Jenna now. For drop-offs, I don't have your nearest locations saved and the rules differ by item, so I'd rather check than guess: paint cans and old printers are usually household hazardous waste or e-waste, and batteries often have separate retail drop-off points. Action: send the Jenna email, then look up City of Toronto drop-off options near Leslieville for paint, electronics and batteries and send you the closest ones with hours.

I can't see Sam's text from here, so I'll pull it up first and see what he said before suggesting anything. Once I know that, I'll find a hotplate-free dinner you can get tonight, like takeout or delivery. Action: read Sam's text about dinner, then give you two or three options that fit and ask which to order.

Happy to. Since Jun's big sister is Ellie, I'll keep everything dairy-free, so no cheese, cheddar snacks or milk chocolate, and nut-free because of Leo's tree nut allergy, checking labels for 'may contain'. I'd think fruit, cut veggies, crackers, popcorn and juice boxes would be enough for three kids. Action: build a PC Express cart with those, look for a 3:00 pickup slot tomorrow (your usual Saturday slot at Loblaws Lakeshore won't apply), and show you the cart before I check out.

Sorry about the heel, morning soreness after a long run is worth getting looked at, so booking is a good call. I'll look for physio openings next week after work and on Saturday, and I'll mention the first-thing-in-the-morning pain when I book. Action: check your calendar and find physio slots next week (evenings) or Saturday, hold the best one, and confirm it with you before booking.

Here's a draft: 'Hey Hannah! Leo and I are heading to Riverdale Park East tomorrow around 10:30 for the playground and the market. Want to come with Ellie and Jun? No pressure if the day's already full.' If we end up grabbing market snacks, I'll keep Ellie's dairy allergy in mind. Action: send it to Hannah at +1 416-555-0163 once you say go.

On it. I'll turn the out-of-office off for tomorrow morning and swap the message to: 'Hi, I'm back but still catching up, so replies may be a little slower than usual. If it's urgent, please let me know. Best, Riya'. Action: switch off the auto-reply for tomorrow morning, update the message with that text, and show you the final wording to approve.

Yes, I can do both. For the photos I'll rename them by date and move the blurry ones into a separate folder rather than deleting anything. For the newsletters, I'll summarize the unopened ones and leave out promos from the senders you unsubscribed from in January (Old Navy, Wayfair, Uber Eats, Lululemon, Dyson). Action: start on the March break photos in Drive, then send you a short digest of this week's unopened newsletters.

Sending the school council reply now. Your Mazda CX-5 is with Intact and renews each April, so I'd start getting quotes about one to two months before renewal, around February or early March, so you have time to compare and can still cancel cleanly. I can't tell you the notice terms for sure without the policy, so I'd check Intact's cancellation terms and your renewal letter instead of guessing. Action: send the reply, pull up the Intact policy documents to confirm notice and cancellation terms, and set a reminder to start quotes.

Your Thursday yard waste pickup resumes Thu 2026-04-09 and then runs every other Thursday, so the next two are April 9 and April 23. Use paper yard waste bags or labelled rigid containers, no plastic, and bundle branches under 7.5 cm, max 1.2 m long and 20 kg. Paper bags are cheapest at Home Depot on Leslie St, a 10-pack for $11.98. Action: add April 9 and April 23 to the shared family calendar (Sam will get the update), unless you'd rather keep them on your own.

Short version: not much is urgent. The one to know about is watermain work on Queen St E between Leslie and Jones starting May 19, with eastbound lane restrictions on weekdays 7am-7pm for about 9 weeks, so expect 501 streetcar delays. The rest is optional: the Leslieville Flea is May 24 at Ashbridge Estate, the movie night poll closes May 31, and Hearth Bakehouse opens May 15. Action: offer to add the May 19 watermain start and the May 24 flea to your calendar, and a reminder for the May 31 poll.

Here's the shape I'd use for the appendix, in your style with short paragraphs, no em dashes and 'merchant' throughout. Fees: Stripe 1.5% (min $0.50), Square 1.75%, Shopify Payments 1.5%, Helcim has no instant product; all flat percentages with no cap. Fee display: net received is the most prominent number in all three. Complaints: 148 posts, with delayed 'sent' payouts (41) and fees on failed payouts (23) the top themes. Real-Time Rail: limited phased launch targeted for 2026, so card-based instant payouts stay the practical rail. Action: write it up as a half-page appendix with a short paragraph for each of the four, using 'use' not 'leverage', and put it in the PRD draft for you to review.

I can check, but I don't have your library account details in front of me right now. Action: look up your Toronto Public Library account for holds that are ready for pickup and tell you the title and branch for each, plus how long each is held.

Got it, I'll move Leo's piano with Mrs. Greene to Fridays at 4:15 pm starting September 2026, since Mondays now clash with your 'Roadmap review - Riya' block. I'll keep the lesson length the same as the current Monday one. Action: update the family calendar with the new Friday series from September, end the Monday series at the end of August, and tell you the first Friday date so Sam sees the change.

Sorry about the dehumidifier. I'll search for the receipt and then check the warranty, since I don't know the brand or exact purchase date yet and many warranties are around a year, which could make last summer borderline. Action: search your email and Drive for a dehumidifier receipt from last summer, then look up the manufacturer's warranty terms and report back whether it's still covered.

For Tom's calendar, I don't have your December plans in front of me, so I'd check before telling you what to block, and I need to confirm any days off you've already planned. For Leo's 'that thing' from last winter's school closure, I don't have a record of it, so I'd rather search your notes and messages than guess. Action: scan your December calendar for travel and school events, list the OOO and early-leave days you'd likely need to block, and also search your notes for the school-closure day last winter.

Partly. Written Portuguese is quite readable if you know Spanish, but spoken Portuguese sounds very different (nasal vowels, softened consonants), so you'll understand more on signs and menus than in conversation. In Lisbon, slow Spanish plus a few key Portuguese phrases usually gets you by, and many people will switch to English. Action: add a short Portuguese cheat sheet (greetings, thanks, ordering, directions) to your Lisbon note.

Good idea to check before Monday rather than rely on memory. I'll go through your sent mail to Tom for anything about roadmap timing and give you his exact wording and dates, so you can see what you actually committed to. Action: search sent mail to Tom for roadmap and timing emails, and send you a short summary with direct quotes.

I'll look at Dr. Lin's availability for Wed 22 April, aiming for late morning. I'll also check your calendar for conflicts at that time before holding anything. Action: check Dr. Lin's openings on April 22 (late morning first), confirm there's no clash on your calendar, then book it and confirm the time with you.

Thanks for the updates, noted all of it. Meetings now go between 9:30 and 16:30, with nothing after 15:00 on Fridays. You get Leo and Jun on Wednesdays and Hannah has Fridays. Spanish with Carlos is Thursdays at 8:00 pm on Zoom for 60 minutes, with your homework review at 19:30, and I'll favour MEC, Indigo and Simons over Amazon. Ms. Alvarez gets contacted through Edsby. Action: update your scheduling rules and calendar with the new meeting hours, Wednesday pickup and Thursday Spanish, and I'll keep to everything else going forward.

Adding the Lumen Pay quarterly planning offsite on 2026-11-12 (Thursday) at the Gladstone House, 9:00 am to 6:00 pm. Two things to flag: Thursdays Leo is in the after-school program until 5:45 pm and the offsite runs to 6:00, so someone else may need to pick him up. Also, the idea of asking Aisha to move the Fri 13 Nov GA retro to Thursday now clashes with the offsite, so that's still unresolved. Action: add the event, then ask you whether Sam can cover Leo's pickup and whether to propose another time for the retro.

I don't have your yard waste pickup schedule saved, and I don't want to guess a date. Action: look up the City of Toronto collection calendar for your address, then add the next two yard waste pickup dates to your calendar and send you the bag and bundling rules.

Yes, I'll build you a one-page drill sheet with three sections: ser vs estar (emotions and locations), por vs para, and the subjunctive after cuando for future events. The last one starts with your own example, corrected: 'Cuando llegue a casa, te llamo.' Each section will have a short rule and about eight fill-in-the-blank sentences, with an answer key on the back. Action: create the sheet in your notes and send it to you before your next lesson.

For Tom's team calendar, I'd block: early leave at 5:00 pm on Thu 10 Dec (Leo's winter concert, which you've already told Tom about), and out of office from Mon 21 Dec through Fri 1 Jan, since you fly out Sun 20 Dec at 22:10 and land back in Toronto Sat 2 Jan. Leo's last school day is Fri 18 Dec, so tell me if you want that afternoon off too. For 'that thing', your snow day list has floor is lava, sock skating relay, blanket fort and more, and Leo wants floor is lava again, but I can't be sure that's the one. Action: add those entries to the team calendar draft for your OK, and ask Leo which game he means.

That sounds exhausting, a packed streetcar both ways with a bag cutting into your shoulder is a lot. Nothing needs doing from my side tonight. Action: I'll hold anything non-urgent until tomorrow so you can put your feet up.

Yay, Lisbon is booked! I'll put the trip on the family calendar so Sam sees it: depart Toronto Pearson on TAP on 2026-12-18 and return 2026-12-30. I don't have the flight numbers, times or booking reference yet. Action: add the trip to the family calendar for those dates, and ask you for the flight times and confirmation code to add to the event.

I'll pull this from the TD joint chequing statements, since that's the household bills account, and check your TD Visa too in case some groceries went on it. I won't touch your EQ Bank savings. Action: read the October, September and August TD statements, total the grocery spending for each month, and send you the three numbers with the comparison.

I'll check your Toronto Public Library account for ready holds, starting with the Leslieville branch and then Pape/Danforth. Your library card expires 2026-02-14, so it's also worth renewing it soon so holds don't lapse. Action: look up your holds, tell you which are ready and where, and set a reminder to renew your card before it expires.

Here's a short draft for Aisha, not sent: 'Hi Aisha, catching up on the readiness doc. Rollback: I'll add the flag name, but who should own weekend flips? Error budget: I'd suggest per day, any objection? Also PAY-1227, the on-call runbook update, has no owner. Can someone on your side take it?' Action: show you the draft and send it to Aisha on Slack once you say go.

I'm sorry, Riya, thinking of you and your dad tomorrow, and a lighter day sounds right. Tomorrow is Wednesday the 18th, and from your usual schedule the likely things to thin are the Payouts standup at 09:45 and your 11:30 weekly 1:1 with Tom, but I'll look at the actual calendar before suggesting anything. I'll keep the evening completely clear for your diya. Action: pull up tomorrow's calendar, list what could be moved, declined or made async, and wait for your OK before changing anything.

A dinosaur trip with Leo sounds great. I'll search for 3-night hotels in Drumheller for March break week (the week of the 16th) and check Royal Tyrrell Museum admission for Leo's age. I need to confirm the exact nights, and whether you're flying into Calgary and renting a car, which affects where to stay. Action: search Drumheller hotels for a 3-night stay in that week, pull Tyrrell child pricing, and ask you to confirm dates and travel before I book anything.

I'm so sorry, Riya. I'll look at tomorrow and clear space so it isn't a sprint, and keep the evening free for your diya. Since you like a lighter schedule around the date each year, I can also set a yearly reminder to protect around March 18. Action: pull up tomorrow's calendar, suggest what to move, decline or shorten, and check with you before changing anything.

Here's a quick checklist for DES-341: does each variant say what the merchant needs to do in plain words, is the tone consistent with the rest of the flow, is the length right for the space, and are the terms accurate. When you give Diego feedback, put it as a Figma comment, not a DM, and frame it as the problem you see, not a rewrite. Action: put this checklist in a note, with comment-ready problem statements for each variant, and remind you after lunch.

Happy to help, but I don't have Sam's birthday or your anniversary date in front of me, and I don't want to guess either. If you tell me the dates and a few things he's been into lately, I can suggest gift ideas and a celebration plan, and work backwards from the anniversary so you're not planning in the last week. Action: ask you for the two dates and his recent interests, then draft a gift shortlist and a timeline with reminders.

Error budget: I'd suggest per day, any objection? Also PAY-1227, the on-call runbook update, has no owner. Can someone on your side take it?' It uses commas and full stops, no em dashes, and keeps each point to one or two sentences. Action: show you the draft and send it on Slack once you approve.

Sure. Before I order, do any of the three kids have allergies or foods to avoid? I'd rather ask than guess. I'm thinking fruit, crackers, veggies with dip and juice boxes. Action: build a PC Express cart with simple snacks for three kids, check for a 3:00 pickup slot tomorrow, and show you the cart plus the allergy question before I check out.

Here's the shape for a half-page appendix. Fees: Stripe 1.5% (min $0.50), Square 1.75%, Shopify Payments 1.5%, Helcim has no instant product, all flat percentages with no cap. Fee display: Stripe, Square and Shopify all make the net-received amount the most prominent number.
